answer.rationale: Memory c2 documents that switching to the low-cost vendor previously delivered sharp unit cost cuts with fast onboarding and accurate invoicing - relevant to the current decisive price gap. Memory c5 records that deferring past quarter end preserved budget flexibility when finance pressure was the driver - a contingency pattern if c2 doesn't transfer cleanly. Intended action: switch primary supply to the low-cost vendor now (14 days to expiry, no auto-renew, and their quote alone meets the 18% mandate). Tighten contract to keep c2's accuracy advantage (clear invoicing/SKU mapping, price-hold clause). Then immediately qualify a second source in parallel as insurance for the 94% line - if the incumbent won't reopen price, sole-source exposure is a delivery-risk problem, but the second source can ramp behind the primary cutover rather than blocking it. Defer and renew-incumbent both fail the cost mandate; negotiate_terms has already been refused by the incumbent.
